# Independent visual/source assessment: W01 destroyed-01 candidate3 (v37)

**Exact subject:** job `1ad3c800-0048-4769-9d27-1cf998f60df6` r1, checkpoint `843073dd…aef5f6`, GLB `f70fd981…2855b5`. These pins match the candidate3 `original-render-evidence.json`.

**Read-only.** I could only read files, so I could not recompute any PNG, GLB or receipt hash. Every hash binding below is the manifest's claim, not something I checked. I wrote nothing. The `research/catalog/...` rubric path doesn't exist, so I used `catalog/rubrics/model-quality/1.0.0.yaml`.

**What I inspected:** all 18 native candidate3 PNGs (six views at 1000, 256 and 128); the matching clean v1-r2 right, left, top and front-three-quarter views at 1000, and right at 256 and front-three-quarter at 128; candidate2 right at 1000 and 256; Hansen, Doha I-14 and Doha I-16. I did not inspect `b23.jpg`, the v37 atlases or previews, the candidate3 export receipt, the camera receipt or the `prospective-operations.json` payload.

## Earlier core defects

| Defect | Candidate3 result |
|---|---|
| Triangular camouflage | **Gone in the views I checked.** At 1000, the right and front-three-quarter views show soft, blobby mottling with no triangles where candidate2 had a dazzle pattern. At 256 no triangles show either. |
| Plank remnant | **Unchanged and still a core objection** (expected, since v37 changes only materials). Right: a flat dashed strip under the wheels. Front-three-quarter: a flat slab on the ground that sticks out past the front of the hull. Rear-three-quarter: a slab sticking out past the rear. Left: the strip shows past both ends of the intact left track. It reads as a loose plank or ladder, not a thrown or collapsed track. |

## Does the new char with grey flecks read as burn or camo?

| Size | Reading |
|---|---|
| **1000** | **Ambiguous; in the side view it leans toward painted pattern.** The flecks are small, evenly sized, cool blue-grey to white, and spread evenly over near-black. The band has hard horizontal top and bottom edges that follow the skirt panel rectangles. Across all six views, that reads like a night or urban disruptive scheme. With three-quarter shading, the front-three-quarter view reads more like soot. |
| **256** | The flecks become grey noise. The band reads as a **dark stripe along the skirt**, which could be burn, dark paint or shadow. It no longer reads specifically as camo, but it doesn't read specifically as burn either. |
| **128** | The flecks disappear. In the right and front-three-quarter views it is a **dark lower band that can't be told apart from shadow under the fender**. Nothing at 128 says "burned". |

**What the sources use to signal burn that candidate3 lacks:**
- **Hansen:** large warm-grey, white and rust patches of bare metal, scorch that crosses panel boundaries, charred turret and hull top, a collapsed track sitting in an ash bed, and debris.
- **Doha I-14:** charred skirt faces with ragged light paint left along the top and edge fringes, char continuing onto the upper hull, collapsed running gear, and ash and debris underneath.
- **Doha I-16:** a darkened burned hull with a pale upper turret.

Hansen's own skirts carry camo-like mottling, so mottling alone doesn't distinguish burn. What candidate3 is missing is everything else: scorch crossing panel edges, ragged paint fringes and warm burnt tones. This is a visual comparison only. It is not a claim about any incident or physical cause.

## Cues view by view, against the protected clean views

- **Right:** Char band, fade at the front end, missing track loop, plank. At 1000 and 256 a **tan rectangle sits in the middle of the band**, between roughly x≈355–432 at 1000. Candidate2 has the same rectangle. I can't attribute it to an owner from renders. There is also a tan strip below the band. Together these break up the continuity of the burn.
- **Front-three-quarter:** Char on the skirt and the side of the rear fender, plus the slab. This is the strongest char view.
- **Front:** The only cue is asymmetric running gear: exposed wheels on one side, an intact track block on the other. The char itself can't be seen.
- **Rear-three-quarter:** The left flank is clean. The only cue is the slab sticking out at the rear.
- **Left (protected):** At 1000 it looks visually the same as clean apart from the extended ground strip. At 128 I can't tell it from clean.
- **Top (protected main surfaces):** The hull and turret look the same as clean. A dark mottled strip runs along the right fender edge. At 1000 it reads as a deposit; at 256 it's a thin dark line; at 128 it's almost invisible.

These are visual comparisons only. They don't verify the protected geometry or the current masks.

## Anchored category scores (observed only; not a formal score)

| Category | Score | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Identity and recognition (core) | **1 (major revision)** | It still reads as an M1-family Abrams in every view at 256. But destroyed-01 does not read as destroyed at 256 or 128 in four of six views. The localized one-flank char reads closer to "damaged" or "dark skirt", which undermines the distinction between damaged and destroyed variants. |
| Silhouette (core) | **2 (serviceable)** | The Abrams silhouette holds. Destroyed-specific silhouette cues are weak, and the plank adds an ambiguous outline. |
| Mechanical and structural coherence (core) | **1 (major revision)** | The plank or slab runs past the hull ends, and the wheels sit on it. It doesn't read as damaged running gear. |
| Proportion and mass | **2 (serviceable)** | The hull and turret keep their clean proportions. The running-gear mass reads oddly. |
| Form hierarchy | **2 (serviceable)** | The band organizes the right flank without overwhelming the silhouette. Its hard edges compete with the panel structure. |
| Surface and material legibility | **2 (serviceable)** | Clearly better than the triangles. Remaining problems: edges bound to panels, cool evenly spaced flecks, the tan interruption, and no warm or retained-paint fringe. |
| Viewpoint robustness | **1 (major revision)** | The condition reads from about two of six views. The left and rear-three-quarter views carry no burn cue at any size. |
| Production integrity (core) | **Not assessed** | — |

## Strongest core objections

1. At gameplay sizes the destroyed condition reads as shadow or a dark skirt rather than burn, and it isn't clearly distinct from a damaged variant.
2. The unchanged plank remnant.
3. At 1000 the char is still partly camo-like: hard panel-bound edges, small evenly spaced cool flecks, and a tan panel in the middle of the band.
4. The condition is confined to one flank, so robustness across views is weak.

## Unassessed technical items and hard gates

**Technical items:** the actual audit of all 181 meshes (the native pass of 181 doesn't substitute for it); protected geometry and masks; protected-owner material definitions and any orphan materials; whether the base factor is actually white `[1,1,1,1]` and the UV mapping is correct; whether the projected tile lands where intended; rubber exclusion; the 24-material and 2-texture budgets as actually built; and the embedded PNG bytes and schemas.

**Hard gates, all unassessed:** current-validation, artifact-integrity (I couldn't hash), deterministic-output (the matching repeat hashes are the manifest's claim), transform-grounding, structural-plausibility (the plank is visually suspect), budgets, explained-content and copying-rights. For required-views, all six views exist and the subject looks complete and unclipped, but the hashes are unverified.

**Comparability caveat:** candidate3's `rendererBundleSha256` (`d063b0b6…`) differs from the bundle used for clean and candidate2 (`5ef8bc32…`). The renderer source hash is the same. Check that the difference doesn't affect material or lighting response before treating these as truly same-frame siblings.

## Status

- **technicalValidation:** pending (native pass only; actual audit not done)
- **visualRecommendation:** none. There is no structured evaluator result, and core objections are unresolved, so this fails closed to no-go.
- **humanApproval:** none

Candidate3 is charged as an autonomous attempt. All earlier failed candidates and their charges stay on record, and nothing is reset or transferred. The char and the right-flank-only damage are a designed finish, not a reproduction of any recorded incident.
